SAS SMALLEST(k, value-1 <, ..., value-n>)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_smallest.Rd

k-th smallest non-missing value. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

k

Positive integer rank: 1 returns the smallest nonmissing value, 2 the second smallest, and so on. If k exceeds the number of nonmissing values the result is missing.

...

Numeric values; missing values are ignored.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

Missing arguments are ignored; the result is missing only when no argument is non-missing. R summary functions return NA unless na.rm = TRUE.

See also

Other descriptive functions: sas_f_cmiss(), sas_f_css(), sas_f_cv(), sas_f_geomean(), sas_f_harmean(), sas_f_kurtosis(), sas_f_largest(), sas_f_max(), sas_f_mean(), sas_f_median(), sas_f_min(), sas_f_n(), sas_f_nmiss(), sas_f_ordinal(), sas_f_pctl(), sas_f_range(), sas_f_skewness(), sas_f_std(), sas_f_stderr(), sas_f_sum(), sas_f_uss(), sas_f_var()

Examples

# SMALLEST: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# SMALLEST(k, ...) returns the k-th smallest nonmissing value; with k = 1 the
# minimum of 3, 9, 5 is 3.
sas_f_smallest(1, 3, 9, 5)  # smallest(1, 3, 9, 5) = 3
#> [1] 3

# Missing values are ignored: with k = 2 the second smallest of 9 and 5 is 9.
sas_f_smallest(2, NA_real_, 9, 5)  # smallest(2, ., 9, 5) = 9
#> [1] 9

# k = 3 exceeds the number of values (2), so the result is missing.
sas_f_smallest(3, 1, 2)  # smallest(3, 1, 2) = .
#> Warning: NOTE: Mathematical operations could not be performed. The result of the operation has been set to a missing value.
#> [1] NA

# With k = 1 but no nonmissing value, the result is missing.
sas_f_smallest(1, NA_real_, NA_real_)  # smallest(1, ., .) = .
#> [1] NA
